subject: physics
question_text: Find the average kinetic energy of a molecule of a gas at 27°C.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 13 Very Short Answer Question 17 (printed p.138). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: average molecular energy = (3/2)k_BT with T = 27°C = 300 K, giving 1.5 × 1.38 × 10⁻²³ × 300 = 6.21 × 10⁻²¹ J, arithmetic verified.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The relation
steps.margin_note: First mark. Write (3/2)k_BT and convert 27°C to 300 K before substituting.
steps.why: This result follows from the kinetic interpretation of temperature — the average translational kinetic energy of a molecule is (3/2)k_BT for any gas, so only the absolute temperature is needed to find it.
common_mistakes: Using k_BT instead of (3/2)k_BT for the average energy of a molecule.
Forgetting to convert 27°C to the absolute scale before substituting.

recall.must_convey: That the average kinetic energy of a molecule is (3/2)k_BT, and 27°C converts to 300 K.
accept: average energy equals three by two k B T
kinetic energy depends only on temperature
heard_as: three by two k B T

steps.memory_tip: Same formula every time: average energy = (3/2)k_BT, whatever the gas.

steps.label: Energy value
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Give the value with the correct power of ten and the unit joule.
steps.why: Substituting k_B = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹ and T = 300 K into (3/2)k_BT gives the numerical value directly by multiplication.
common_mistakes: Losing track of the power of ten and reporting 6.21 × 10⁻²² J or 6.21 × 10⁻²⁰ J.
Omitting the unit joule after writing the numeric value.

recall.must_convey: That the average kinetic energy comes out to 6.21 times 10 to the minus 21 joule.
accept: six point two one e minus twenty one joule
reject: average energy equals three by two k B T

insider_note: Keep the power of ten straight through the multiplication — a slipped exponent is the most common way this mark is lost.
